standard.title: Digital systems and components
standard.description: identify and explore digital systems and their components for a purpose
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise and explore digital systems (hardware and software) for a purpose (AC9TDIFK01). They have identified some hardware and software components used for familiar purposes. They have not yet identified components by name or explained how component combinations enable a system's purpose.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify digital systems in familiar contexts and explain how components (input, output, storage, processing) work together to serve a purpose.

nodes.label: What digital systems are
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify familiar digital systems (devices) in their home and school environment and name what they are used for
nodes.minimum_width: Name at least two different digital systems encountered at home or school and state a purpose for each
nodes.typical_width: Identify multiple digital systems (tablet, computer, TV, interactive display, camera) in familiar settings; explain how each is used at home or school
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australians in remote communities access and use digital systems for essential services — identifying specific systems and the communities they serve
Compare digital systems used at school with those used at home — identify which system is used for each purpose and why they may differ

response_modes.reason: Students often conflate the term 'computer' with all digital systems, missing that a TV remote, tablet, and interactive whiteboard are all distinct digital systems. Encountering a range of contexts (home, school, community) helps students build a reliable category for 'digital system' rather than a narrow exemplar.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The First Nations remote community direction offers genuine richness — it connects digital systems to community need and service access, making the 'purpose' dimension of the descriptor meaningful beyond personal use cases.
success_criteria: Names at least two different digital systems correctly
States a distinct purpose for each system

nodes.label: Components of digital systems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and name components of digital systems — including input devices, output devices and storage
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and name at least one input and one output component on a familiar digital system; explain what each component does
nodes.typical_width: Identify input devices (keyboard, touchpad, camera, microphone), output devices (screen, speakers, printer) and storage on common digital systems; explain the function of each component type
wider: Explore how the same component serves different purposes on different devices — for example how a screen is both output on a laptop and also input (touch) on a tablet
Investigate a camera on a device: identify it as an input component and explain how it enables different purposes (photos, video calls, scanning)

response_modes.reason: Component naming requires accurate recall and correct categorisation (input/output/storage). Students commonly swap input and output. Practice across multiple devices — naming and categorising components repeatedly — builds the precision needed before they can reason about how components combine.

success_criteria: Correctly names at least one input and one output component on a digital system
Explains what each named component does in plain language
nodes.hinge_reason: Component categorisation errors (swapping input/output) propagate directly into Node 3 — students who cannot reliably identify and categorise components cannot explain how they coordinate to serve a purpose.

nodes.label: Components working together for a purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explore how components of a digital system work together to serve a specific purpose
nodes.minimum_width: For one familiar digital system, identify the components used and explain how they work together to achieve the system's purpose
nodes.typical_width: Explain how components (input, output, processing, storage) work together across different digital systems for different purposes — for example how a camera, screen and storage combine to let you take and keep a photo
wider: Compare how a tablet and a desktop computer achieve the same purpose (e.g. writing a message) using different component combinations — explain why the components differ
Investigate how digital systems provide communities with services — for example how input, processing and output components combine to allow TV to reach remote communities

response_modes.reason: Component identification and purpose identification are component understandings. At this node students must coordinate both simultaneously — identifying which components are active and explaining how their coordination produces the purpose. This is the integration of the descriptor's two demands: 'identify components' and 'for a purpose'.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The community services direction — especially the remote community TV access elaboration — makes the 'for a purpose' demand genuinely rich. Students move from personal use to community-scale purpose, which broadens the concept substantially.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two components used in a specific digital system
Explains how those components work together to achieve the system's purpose
